edits.new_text: The DAS claim's Gemma version is therefore supported at every rank by the random-subspace, permuted-label and untrained-network controls; the dormancy checks (reverse interchange, projected-map retention) were not run, a recovery of 1.98 to 2.81 times the full-state swap is the off-manifold signature Makelov et al. [122] warn about, and the Qwen3-8B and Gemma controls used different objectives, readouts and permutation schemes, so their outcomes are not directly comparable (Table 364d) (iteration-8 correction).

edits.old_text: and the subspace holds 0.0009 of the twin's natural variance across prompts, at the random 95th percentile.

### 7.8.4 A dose dial that keeps the programs

edits.old_text: | Gemma claims | Temperature law holds; DAS controls hold, calling it one dimensional not licensed; 7 to 8 of 10 circuit nodes validated | Error 0.026; random initialisation at most 0.25 times; dose dial 42 correct BFS against 35 for the instruction |

edits.old_text: In Gemma the analogous subspace at the fork passes all three controls and acts as a dose dial that keeps the programs.
edits.new_text: In Gemma the analogous subspace at the fork passes the random-subspace, permuted-label and untrained-network controls (dormancy checks not run; its natural variance lies below the random 95th percentile at ranks 1, 2 and 4, and it recovers 1.98 to 2.81 times the full-state swap) and, with the shared opening prefilled, acts as a dose dial that keeps the programs; the Qwen3-8B and Gemma controls used different objectives, readouts and permutation schemes, so their outcomes are not directly comparable (iteration-8 correction).

edits.old_text: In Gemma, DAS at the fork passes the controls with random subspaces, permuted labels and an untrained network, but the subspace is not unique across seeds and the committed rule does not license calling it one dimensional; as a dose dial it raises correct BFS programs from 11 to 42 of 50, above the 35 of an explicit BFS instruction, while a difference-in-means edit toward BFS at matched teacher-forced effect destroys the programs.
edits.new_text: In Gemma, DAS at the fork passes the controls with random subspaces, permuted labels and an untrained network (dormancy checks not run; its natural variance lies below the random 95th percentile at ranks 1, 2 and 4), but the subspace is not unique across seeds and the committed rule does not license calling it one dimensional; the Qwen3-8B and Gemma controls used different objectives, readouts and permutation schemes, so their outcomes are not directly comparable. With the shared opening prefilled, the edit raises correct BFS from 11 to 42 of 50; the instruction, sampled without the prefill, gives 35, which is not comparable; a difference-in-means edit toward BFS at matched teacher-forced effect destroys the programs (iteration-8 correction).
